Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 200 + 600 = 800 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 50 × (5/18) = 250/18 = 125/9 m/s

⇒ Time = 800 ÷ (125/9)

⇒ Time = (800 × 9) ÷ 125

⇒ Time = 7200 ÷ 125 = 57.6 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 57.6 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the **same direction**, the relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, the relative speed is the **sum** of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).</p

questions.question: Simplify: sqrt{121 times 49} + sqrt{64 times 36} - sqrt{100 times 16}

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can separate the square roots directly using the property √(a × b) = √a × √b:

⇒ (11 × 7) + (8 × 6) − (10 × 4)

⇒ 77 + 48 − 40

⇒ 125 − 40 = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(121 × 49) + √(64 × 36) − √(100 × 16)

**Formula Used:**

√(x × y) = √x × √y

**Calculation:**

⇒ √(121 × 49) = √121 × √49 = 11 × 7 = 77

⇒ √(64 × 36) = √64 × √36 = 8 × 6 = 48

⇒ √(100 × 16) = √100 × √16 = 10 × 4 = 40

Substituting the calculated values back into the main expression:

⇒ 77 + 48 − 40

⇒ 125 − 40

⇒ 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the strict sequence of Brackets, Order (Powers/Roots), Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction from left to right to ensure an accurate result.

Properties of Radicals

The product of two square roots is equivalent to the square root of their product: √a × √b = √(a × b). This property is universally valid for all non-negative real numbers.

Common Perfect Squares

questions.question: What is the smallest natural number that should be added to 9054 such that a remainder of 6 is left when the resulting number is divided by each of the numbers 28, 24, 56 and 29?

Find **LCM** of 28, 24, 56, and 29.

Multiples of 4872 near 9054: 4872 × 2 = 9744.

Required number = (Next Multiple + Remainder) − Given Number = (9744 + 6) − 9054 = 9750 − 9054 = 696.

**∴ The correct answer is 696.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ 29 = 29 (Prime number)

⇒ 4872 × 2 = 9744

⇒ To leave a remainder of 6: 9744 + 6 = 9750

⇒ Smallest number to be added = 9750 − 9054 = 696

LCM and Remainder Concept

The general form of a number that leaves a remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z is [k × **LCM**(x, y, z) + r].

questions.question: The expenditure of Sudha is 100% more than her savings. If her expenditure decreases by 4% and savings increase by 35%, then by what percent does her income increase?4736
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** = 200 : 100 = 2 : 1

Using **Alligation/Weighted Average** method:

Net Income change = (Expenditure % × E-ratio + Savings % × S-ratio) ÷ (E-ratio + S-ratio)

Income increase = (−4% × 2 + 35% × 1) ÷ (2 + 1) = (−8 + 35) ÷ 3 = 27 ÷ 3 = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Expenditure** is 100% more than **Savings**.

**Formula Used:** **Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc7c79c83b2750860cc181cf636b11cc6435cf6ad677768b8109949908503019.png] 

⇒ Let **Savings** = 100

⇒ **Expenditure** = 100 + 100% of 100 = 200

⇒ Initial **Income** = 200 + 100 = 300

⇒ New **Expenditure** = 200 − 4% of 200 = 200 − 8 = 192

⇒ New **Savings** = 100 + 35% of 100 = 135

⇒ New **Income** = 192 + 135 = 327

⇒ Increase in **Income** = 327 − 300 = 27

⇒ % Increase = (27 ÷ 300) × 100 = 9%

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The fundamental identity is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any percentage change in two components directly determines the change in the third.

Weighted Average Concept

If components **A** and **B** change by **x%** and **y%**, the total change is **(A×x + B×y) ÷ (A+B)**. This is the fastest way to solve income-expenditure problems.

Percentage Base Change

When a value is **x%** more than another, the ratio is **(100+x) : 100**. Always identify the base correctly before calculating increments or decrements.</p

questions.question: The area of a rectangle gets reduced by 21 m² if its length is reduced by 7 m and breadth is increased by 5 m and if its length is increased by 4 m and breadth is increased by 5 m, the area is increased by 67 m². Find the original area of the rectangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let **Length** = L and **Breadth** = B.

From conditions: (L − 7)(B + 5) = LB − 21 ⇒ 5L − 7B = 14

From second condition: (L + 4)(B + 5) = LB + 67 ⇒ 5L + 4B = 47

Subtracting both: 11B = 33 ⇒ B = 3 m. Putting B in first: 5L − 21 = 14 ⇒ 5L = 35 ⇒ L = 7 m.

**Original Area** = L × B = 7 × 3 = 21 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 21 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Reduction in area = 21 m², Increase in area = 67 m².

**Formula:** Area of Rectangle = Length (L) × Breadth (B).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b47681f904bf6fd3d08dcb7685f7305c0fb10bc60b23d5a42c393182c4fb92a.png] 
⇒ Case 1: (L − 7)(B + 5) = LB − 21

⇒ LB + 5L − 7B − 35 = LB − 21

⇒ 5L − 7B = 14 ----(i)

⇒ Case 2: (L + 4)(B + 5) = LB + 67

⇒ LB + 5L + 4B + 20 = LB + 67

⇒ 5L + 4B = 47 ----(ii)

⇒ Subtracting (i) from (ii): (5L + 4B) − (5L − 7B) = 47 − 14

⇒ 11B = 33 ⇒ B = 3 m

⇒ Substituting B in (i): 5L − 7(3) = 14 ⇒ 5L − 21 = 14 ⇒ 5L = 35 ⇒ L = 7 m

⇒ Area = 7 × 3 = 21 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 21 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total boundary length is given by P = 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The length of the diagonal is calculated using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(L² + B²).

Percentage Change in Area

If length changes by x% and breadth by y%, net area change % = x + y + (xy/100).</p

questions.question: Under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025, how many days of statutory wage employment are guaranteed per rural household per financial year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**125 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025** is a significant legislative framework designed to enhance rural livelihood by guaranteeing **125 days** of **statutory wage employment** per **financial year** to every **rural household**.
 
• The primary objective of this act is to provide a robust **social security** net for families residing in **rural areas**, ensuring that at least one member of the household can find work when needed.
 
• This guarantee applies to all **adult members** of a **rural household** who volunteer to perform **unskilled manual work**.
 
• Under the provisions of the act, the **125 days** of work is a **legal entitlement**, representing an increase from the previously standard **100 days** offered under earlier schemes like **MGNREGA**.
 
• The act emphasizes **inclusive growth**, specifically targeting **vulnerable groups**, including **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **women**, to ensure they have access to **minimum income** through labor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vision of Viksit Bharat 2047:**

 
 
• The **Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act 2025** is a foundational step toward the **Viksit Bharat 2047** vision, which aims to transform **India** into a **developed nation** by the **100th year** of its **independence**.
 
• By increasing the **employment days** to **125**, the government aims to reduce **rural-to-urban migration** and strengthen the **rural economy**.
 
 
 
• **Financial Provisions and Wages:**
 
 
• Wages under this act are revised annually and are linked to the **Consumer Price Index-Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL)** to protect workers against **inflation**.
 
• The **Central Government** typically bears **100%** of the **wage cost** for **unskilled manual labor**, while **material costs** are shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in a **75:25 ratio**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Work Permitted:**
 
 
• The act focuses on the creation of **durable assets** such as **water conservation structures**, **check dams**, **rural roads**, and **afforestation** projects.
 
• Work is also directed toward **natural resource management** and **individual assets** for **small and marginal farmers** to improve **agricultural productivity**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Implementation:**
 
 
• The scheme utilizes the **G RAM G portal** for **real-time monitoring**, **e-attendance** via the **National Mobile Monitoring System (NMMS)**, and **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to ensure transparency.
 
• **Aadhaar-Based Payment Systems (ABPS)** are mandatory to ensure that the **wages** reach the correct **bank accounts** of the **beneficiaries** without **leakage**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unemployment Allowance:** If the **government** fails to provide **employment** within **15 days** of the **application for work**, the applicant is legally entitled to a daily **unemployment allowance**.
 
• **Social Audit:** To maintain **accountability**, the **Gram Sabha** is empowered to conduct **social audits** of all the **projects** executed under the **Act** in the **Gram Panchayat**.
 
• **Workplace Facilities:** The act mandates that **facilities** such as **drinking water**, **shade** for periods of rest, and **first-aid boxes** must be provided at every **worksite**.
 
• **Role of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs):** The **Gram Panchayats** are responsible for **planning** and **implementing** at least **50%** of the works in terms of **cost**, ensuring **decentralized governance**.

• Initially established under the **Government of India Act 1919**, the commission was intended to fulfill the functions of recruitment and to protect the interests of public servants from political influences.

• It was established in **February 1964** based on the recommendations of the **Santhanam Committee** on Prevention of Corruption.
 
• It was originally a non-statutory body but was granted **statutory status** by the **CVC Act, 2003**.

• **Transactree Technologies Private Limited**, which operates as a **Non-Banking Financial Company-Peer to Peer (NBFC-P2P)** lending platform (widely known as **Lendbox**), was penalised for non-compliance with the **Peer-to-Peer Lending Platform (Reserve Bank) Directions, 2017**.
 
• These regulatory actions were taken under the provisions of **Section 47A** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, and relevant sections of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The **RBI** clarified that these penalties are based on **deficiencies in regulatory compliance** and are not intended to validate any specific transactions between these entities and their customers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Transactree Technologies** operates **Lendbox**, which is a leading **fintech** player in the **Indian** credit market.
 
 
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**:
 
 
• It is the minimum percentage of **deposits** that a **commercial bank** has to maintain in the form of **liquid cash**, **gold**, or **unencumbered securities**.
 
• It is a key **monetary policy** tool used by the **RBI** to control the **expansion of bank credit** and ensure the **solvency** of banks.

• It performs the function of the **Monetary Authority**, the **Regulator and Supervisor of the financial system**, and the **Manager of Foreign Exchange**.
 
• Under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, the **RBI** has the power to inspect **banking companies** and impose fines to maintain **financial stability** in the **Indian economy**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight**:
 
 
• The **RBI** frequently issues **Master Directions** on **Know Your Customer (KYC)**, **Cyber Security Framework**, and **Interest Rate on Deposits** to protect the interests of depositors.

• **Operation Spot Trap** was a massive state-wide anti-corruption drive conducted in **January 2025** to weed out bribery and financial irregularities in public offices.
 
• The operation was orchestrated by the **Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB)** of **Kerala**, following numerous complaints regarding "speed money" or illegal commissions being demanded for public services.
 
• A total of **36 people**, including several **government employees** and private **middlemen**, were arrested during the coordinated raids across multiple districts. ***Hence, the statement regarding the location being Kerala is correct.***
 
• The raids primarily targeted departments with high public interaction, such as the **Revenue Department**, **Motor Vehicles Department (MVD)**, and **Local Self-Government (LSG)** institutions.

• **Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB):**

• The agency is headed by a Director of the rank of **Director General of Police (DGP)** or **Additional Director General of Police (ADGP)**.
 
• Its primary function is to conduct "trap" operations, surprise checks, and detailed enquiries into assets disproportionate to the known sources of income of **government employees**.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Trap Operations:**
 
 
• A "trap" typically involves the use of **phenolphthalein-coated currency notes**. When a public servant accepts this money, their hands are dipped in a sodium carbonate solution, which turns pink, providing scientific evidence of the bribe-taking act.
 
• **Operation Spot Trap** utilized these methods along with advanced surveillance to catch offenders red-handed in **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
